title: A refusal stop reason returns no content blocks and reads as a finished turn
claim: An agent loop that decides a turn is complete because the response contained no tool-use blocks cannot distinguish a refusal from a finished answer, and will record the refusal's empty text as the agent's output.
appliesTo: Any agent loop driving a completion API with tools, where the exit condition is the absence of tool-use blocks rather than an explicit check of the stop reason.
expectation: A refused request fails loudly — an error status, a thrown exception, or at minimum a text block saying the request was declined — so a loop that keeps calling until the model stops asking for tools will notice.
reality: The response is a normal 200 carrying stop_reason 'refusal', content: [], and output_tokens: 0. There is no exception to catch and no text to read. A loop whose exit test is 'no tool_use blocks were returned' takes that as a completed turn, extracts an empty string as the answer, and proceeds. Downstream the empty string is scored, tallied, or reported like any other result.
mechanism: Refusal is a terminal stop reason rather than a transport or API error, so the SDK resolves the promise normally. The content array is empty because nothing was generated, and every structural test a loop is likely to apply — did it ask for a tool, did it return text — is satisfied by absence rather than by evidence.
workaround: Test the stop reason explicitly and treat 'refusal' as its own outcome, distinct from both success and error. In an eval, count refusals in a separate column and exclude them from the denominator; a refused arm that silently scores zero is worse than a crashed one, because it looks like a measurement. Refusal is also condition-dependent rather than deterministic: identical tasks differing only in the tool list were refused in one arm and answered in the other, so an A/B comparison can lose exactly one side.

evidence.command: messages.create({ model, max_tokens: 6000, tools: [bash], messages: [{ role: 'user', content: task }] })
evidence.note: The task asked an agent to determine whether a named third-party production API was down. Three control trials returned this; the treatment arm, identical but for one extra tool definition, was not refused and answered normally.

check.command: Send a request the model will decline, with tools attached, and inspect stop_reason and content.length rather than only testing for tool-use blocks.
check.confirmedIf: the call resolves without throwing, stop_reason is 'refusal', and content is empty
check.refutedIf: the call raises an error, returns a non-2xx status, or returns a text block explaining the refusal

observations.note: Found while running a two-arm retrieval experiment. The control arm was refused on all three trials and produced no tool calls and no answer; the harness recorded three empty results and printed a tally as though the arm had been measured. The refusal was only visible after probing stop_reason directly. Rewriting the task to ask about a neutral host instead of a named third-party production service reduced it but did not remove it: one of three control trials on the rewritten task was still refused. It is condition-dependent, not deterministic.

environment.note: Anthropic Messages API via @anthropic-ai/sdk, tools attached, adaptive thinking enabled.

triggers: agent loop until no tool_use blocks were returned
eval arm refused and scored as a measurement
